## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**:把 `sql-driver.ts` 里「按日/周/月/季/年分组时,各数据库方言生成什么 SQL 分桶表达式」这一个机制(`buildDateBucketExpr` 的方法体)原样搬进新建的 `sql-driver-date-bucket.ts`;类上的方法、文档注释和签名全部保留,只把方法体转交过去,宿主接口 `DateBucketHost` 恰好列出方法体读的 6 个成员。
- **为什么改**:#25521 拆分超大文件的第 20 刀;第 19 刀合入后重新测量,这是仍成「一个机制」、收益最大且不碰任何系列限制的区域,`sql-driver.ts` 减少 39 行。
- **风险与回滚**:纯搬移,无行为变化;三个 SQL 驱动的测试两端逐条一致,公开类型声明哈希不变,344 条探针读数两端一致(仅 1 条栈顶接收者名不同)。回滚即还原本 PR。
- **先看**:`sql-driver-date-bucket.ts`(头注释、`DateBucketHost`、函数体);`sql-driver.ts` 中 `buildDateBucketExpr` 的转交桩;`sql-driver.ts` 新增的 3 行 import。
- **两分钟验证**:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/driver-sql exec vitest run src/sql-driver-date-bucket.test.ts src/sql-driver-21485-date-bucket-calendar-day.test.ts src/sql-driver-temporal-dialect.test.ts`,预期全部通过。
- **需要你做的**:无,席位落地。

## What changes

Cut 20 of the `sql-driver.ts` split (#24586 ruling A, recorded in `6270097840`). The claim is `6456805734`. Cut 19 (#26960) merged first, as `d7f76b6d97`; this cut opens with a fresh seam table taken on `origin/main` `6845035c6b` (below) and takes the largest area that is one mechanism and moves cleanly: **date bucketing**, `buildDateBucketExpr`, from the class head. Its body moves unedited into a **new** seam module, `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-date-bucket.ts`, through its host `DateBucketHost`.

`buildDateBucketExpr` is the per-dialect SQL fragment a date dimension groups by at `day`, `week`, `month`, `quarter` or `year`: PostgreSQL `to_char`, MySQL `date_format`, SQLite `strftime`, with the #21485 calendar-day arm for a `Field.date` and the #21595 Thursday-rule ISO week on SQLite. It returns `null` for a granularity the dialect does not model. Its two callers stay in the class: `aggregate` (the GROUP BY) and `dateBucketSql` (the printed form `service-analytics` echoes).

**Why a new module.** No existing seam module holds anything about aggregation or temporal read expressions; the nearest (`sql-driver-schema-sync.ts`) is DDL. The new module imports `sql-driver.ts` for a type only (`import type { SqlDriver }`), so it adds no evaluation cycle, and the body reads no module-level declaration, so nothing gains `export` and nothing else moves.

**`DateBucketHost`** lists exactly the six members the body reads, each typed as the class member (`SqlDriver['NAME']`): the `isPostgres`, `isMysql` and `isSqlite` flags and the protected `dateGranularityCapabilities` getter (as getters), and the protected `temporalFieldKind` and `sqliteTemporalArg` methods (as late-bound closures). All six are read by members that stay as well.

The change is move-only, and the card stays open for later cuts. There is no `docs/adr/**` edit, no `packages/spec/**` edit, no anchor entry change, no gate edit, no test edit and no new gate. Branch `claude/project-thread-p875md` (the platform assigned it to this card thread, as the claim records). The move is one commit, `7c6f6f1fe`, on `6845035c6b`.

**Net line count (the seat's rule).** `sql-driver.ts` goes from 18,406 lines to 18,367: **-39**.

- **Out:** the body, 56 lines.
- **In:** the stub body, 14 lines, and 3 import lines (a 2-line comment and the `./sql-driver-date-bucket.js` import, placed after cut 16's seam import).
- `sql-driver-date-bucket.ts` is new: 119 lines (a 40-line header, the type import, the 15-line host and the function with its one-line docblock).

**Path readers.** No test, script, doc, ADR or anchor entry reads the body by path, so none is migrated (screen below).

**Serial with the file's in-flight PRs.** I read the file list of every open PR on `objectstack-ai/objectstack` at the start (41) and again before opening this one (26). None touches `packages/drivers/driver-sql/**`.

### Pricing the areas

Eligibility is as cuts 11-19 defined it: an annotated return type or not public; no `getBuilder`, `this.FIELD.delete/insert/update(`, private-static, `super`, bare-`this` or `this`-write site; not `insertOnlyUpsertColumns`; not a member pinned in place (`createColumn`, `applyFilterCondition`, `formatInput`/`formatOutput`, `initObjects`, `ensureShardTable`, `computeTenantField`, `migrateMysqlDatetimeColumns`/`migrateMysqlTimeColumns`, `compileFilters`). Each area is priced per mechanism (cut 19's correction), as its stubs minus its bodies, then net of its import edits. The two leading rows were measured by running the move script on a scratch copy of the file; the rest are the stub estimate (a stub costs 4 lines, +2 per field read, +1 per method read).

## Why

### Why this area, as one area

- **One mechanism.** One method answers one question: "what SQL expression does this dialect group a date field by at this granularity". Its two callers and every member it reads stay in the class.
- **It pays the most of any single mechanism that moves cleanly** (-39 measured, against about -34 for the runner-up).
- **No series limit is touched.** The body builds through no `getBuilder`, reads no static, has no `this.FIELD.delete/insert/update(` site, uses no `super` or bare `this`, and assigns nothing to `this`. The method is protected with an annotated return type (`{ sql: string; bindings: any[] } | null`). `check:tenant-chokepoint`'s D8 predicates, measured with its own `nullArmsOf`: **4 at base and 4 at head**, all in `sql-driver.ts`, 0 in the moved body and 0 in the module.
- **Durability gate.** The body has no `try` and calls no `logDurabilityFailure`. `check:durability-log-level --list` prints 165 lines at both ends, identical except that two `runWideningAlters` seams in `sql-driver.ts` move 39 lines up and `logDurabilityFailure`'s line 3 down (the import).
- **Subclasses and spies.** `TursoDriver` overrides neither the method nor a member it reads. `SqliteWasmDriver` overrides the `isSqlite` getter; the host reads `isSqlite` through a getter on the driver at call time, so the override is still the one the body reads, and `sqlite-wasm-driver-date-bucket.test.ts` (in the wasm suite above) pins the SQL that driver emits. `turso-driver.ts` names `SqlDriver.buildDateBucketExpr` in prose, still true. The dogfood `date-bucket-parity-turso.test.ts` redefines `buildDateBucketExpr` on an instance and `sql-driver-temporal-dialect.test.ts` calls it through `(d as any)`; both still reach the method, which is still on the class.
- **Path readers, screened.** No script, test, doc or ADR names the member by a `sql-driver.ts#…` pointer or a `sql-driver.ts::…` key, and no `scripts/adr-anchors/**` record names it or date bucketing.

## The shape (#23050 shape B, as cuts 1-19 apply it)

- The class method keeps its docblock and signature, byte-identical. Its body is now one host literal plus `buildDateBucketExpr.call(host, field, granularity, table)`, marked `[#25521 cut 20]`. The method is synchronous at both ends, so a failure is still a synchronous throw (probe reading 7).
- The fields go as GETTERS that read the driver at call time, and the methods as closures that call them on the driver at call time. So a subclass override, an instance spy, or a getter overridden in a subclass is still the one the body reaches (probe readings 3, 4, 5).
- **Comments.** The module header says what moved, what stayed and how the body reaches the class. The `sql-driver.ts` import comment names cut 20 in 2 lines. Neither cites an `ADR-NNNN` letter. The method's docblock (which cites ADR-0053) stays in `sql-driver.ts`.
- **How the move was made.** A script produced it from the source text; nothing was retyped. Each body line is re-indented two columns; no body line starts inside a template literal.

## Verification

### ADR anchors

- **The count.** `check:adr-anchors` counts **1900** decision-letter citations at base `6845035c6b` (a clean detached worktree) and **1900** at the move commit, over 91 anchored files at both ends; the two outputs are byte-identical. Both runs exit 0.

- **No entry needs a new home.** No anchor entry names the moved member. `check:adr-symbol-anchors` output is byte-identical at both ends.
- **After `main` moved.** `main` moved 20 commits under the cut (to `07d18e692`, none in `packages/drivers/**`). Its tip counts **1900** letters (a clean detached worktree), and so does a local, unpushed merge of the move commit with it; both exit 0. I did not merge `main` into this branch: `git merge-tree --write-tree` of the head with it exits 0, so the tree is not stale.

### The published `.d.ts` does not change

This is measured under the series bar (ruling `6348891160`, item 1).

- **How each end was built.** `pnpm turbo run build --filter=@objectstack/driver-sql --force` at each end, against the same dependency tree. The base leg writes base `sql-driver.ts` into this worktree and removes the new module, under an EXIT/INT/TERM trap that restores HEAD. The restore is proved by the HEAD blob hashes, an empty `git diff HEAD` and 0 status entries (`RESTORE-OK fb5f2d3313… 0bb2ccab65…`).
- **The hashes.** The raw sha256 of `dist/index.d.ts` and `dist/index.d.mts` is the same at base and at the move commit: `0f33bf3febaac3c7aa96f68a4226d752766b8203ab7acade523b69f9aaa44d74` (unchanged since cut 8). These two are the dist's only declaration files (no chunk), so the declaration-reorder bar of ruling `6441032442` does not come into play.
- **Positive control.** I dropped `protected` from `buildDateBucketExpr` in a copy of the head `index.d.ts` (1 hit, then 0). The copy hashes to `1fda05673f202a32293501dc46b90afa75edd56c1dc632f66d4699af09ef3197`, with `cmp` exit 1.
- **Export lists.** CJS `require` of each dist gives 59 names (sha1 `05757ce5ae` at both ends); the ESM namespace of `index.mjs` gives the same 59 at both ends (sha1 `05757ce5ae`). Neither the moved function nor `DateBucketHost` is among them.
- **The head dist carries the move.** `.call(host` sites in `index.mjs` go from 69 at base to 70 at head (the stub).

- **The stub.** Leading trivia (the docblock), modifiers and the signature are identical to base.
- **The class.** It has 350 members at both ends, in the same order, and the 349 unmoved members are byte-identical, trivia included.

- **Late-binding probe.** A scratch script, not committed. It runs node against each end's built dist and prints 344 readings, each with the result or the error's class, message and top stack frame:
  1. `buildDateBucketExpr` on SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL and MSSQL drivers (never connected), for all five granularities plus `hour` and none, over a declared `date`, `datetime`, `time` and `text` field, an undeclared field, and no / an unknown table;
  2. the SQLite legacy-datetime repair arm (`sqliteTemporalArg`'s other branch);
  3. a SUBCLASS overriding the `isSqlite` / `isPostgres` getters, and one overriding `dateGranularityCapabilities` (the overrides are the ones read);
  4. subclass overrides of `temporalFieldKind` (PostgreSQL, MySQL) and of `sqliteTemporalArg` (likewise);
  5. instance spies on `temporalFieldKind` and `sqliteTemporalArg` (they are the ones the body reaches, with the arguments recorded);
  6. `knex` replaced on the instance after construction, then restored;
  7. a failure inside the body (a throwing `temporalFieldKind`; an undefined capability row): synchronous throws;
  8. the callers: `dateBucketSql` on three dialects, and real SQLite `aggregate` GROUP BYs over a `date` and a `datetime` field at all five granularities;
  9. the method's shape on the prototype (type, arity).
- **Probe result.** 343 of the 344 readings are identical. The other one is reading 7's undefined capability row, which differs only in the top stack frame's receiver name: `NullCaps.buildDateBucketExpr` at base and `Object.buildDateBucketExpr` at head. That is shape B's receiver, the same at every earlier cut, and no test or consumer reads it.
- **Not run.** No ablation, because no tested behaviour changed.
- **`test:repo`.** Not run locally; it is CI's run on this PR.

## Acceptance notes

- **`check:tenant-chokepoint`'s `SCAN_FILES` does not list `sql-driver-date-bucket.ts`.** The moved body holds 0 tenant predicates and builds no query (it returns `{ sql, bindings }` text). Noted, not filed: widening `SCAN_FILES` would be a gate change.
- **Stale links.** `sql-driver.ts` has the same 30 `{@link X}` sites (21 names) that are neither a top-level binding nor a `SqlDriver` member at base and at head (the name set is identical). The module has none.
- **The series' remaining yield, priced on this base.** After this cut, one single mechanism still pays more than -30: the presumed-timestamp update (`updateWithPresumedTimestamp` with `resolveUpdatedAtColumnPresence`, -37 in bodies, about -34 with a new module's import). Everything else is -29 or less per mechanism, or pinned or blocked by a series limit (the MySQL widenings, the tenant members, the private-static readers).
